device.name: Sunblaze CartPole-v0 (deterministic classic control)
device.vendor: UC Berkeley, Intel Labs and contributors

facts.text: The registered entry point of SunblazeCartPole-v0 is sunblaze_envs.classic_control:ModifiableCartPoleEnv
ModifiableCartPoleEnv subclasses gym's CartPoleEnv and the package's EnvBinarySuccessMixin
SunblazeCartPole-v0 is registered with max_episode_steps=200 and reward_threshold=195.0
EnvRegistry.make wraps an environment that has a timestep limit in sunblaze_envs.time_limit.TimeLimit
sunblaze_envs.make delegates to the package's own EnvRegistry
The package's TimeLimit resets its elapsed-step counter to 0 on reset
ModifiableCartPoleEnv.reset sets nsteps=0 and returns the parent Gym reset()
ModifiableCartPoleEnv.step increments nsteps and returns the parent Gym step()
is_success returns True once nsteps reaches 195, the package's definition of a balanced episode
The documented deterministic CartPole parameters are force 10, length 0.5 and mass 0.1
The commented parent defaults recorded in the clone are gravity 9.8, masscart 1.0, masspole 0.1, length 0.5 (half the pole's length), force_mag 10.0 and tau 0.02 s between state updates
CartPoleEnv is imported from gym.envs.classic_control.cartpole, so the action space, the observation bounds and the failure thresholds are Gym's and are not stated by this repository
setup.py pins gym==0.10.8r1, the legacy Gym API the environment is built on
The README documents sunblaze_envs.make('SunblazeCartPole-v0') as the construction path for the deterministic CartPole

determinism.notes: a reset seed fixes the fake's initial state and the dynamics are deterministic, so the fake repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the upstream reset takes new, not seed (classic_control.py:52-56), and the bridge falls back to Gym's legacy seed() before reset(); the fake uses Python's random.Random while Gym uses numpy's generator, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: rigid-body equations of motion of a cart and a pole on a frictionless track inherited from Gym; no contacts, no friction and no actuator, sensor or noise model, and the push is an ideal step force

the clone states no failure thresholds, and the base class calls Gym's reset (classic_control.py:52-56); the randomized variants draw the initial state from -0.05 to 0.05 (classic_control.py:296-299), and the fake uses that spread as a placeholder together with placeholder thresholds, so its trajectories are not compared with the upstream environment
the fake integrates with Python floats and random.Random, while Gym 0.10.8 uses numpy arrays and its own random generator; one seed gives different trajectories on the two

the 200-step TimeLimit is re-implemented in the fake and reported through the legacy 4-tuple done flag, so the bridge marks the limit as terminated; upstream's limit is the wrapper in sunblaze_envs/time_limit.py:4-10 added by the package registry
no rendering and no PassiveEnvChecker; the fake has no close() because the upstream class inherits one from Gym, which is outside the clone and was not run
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks only advance simulated time by timestep_ms (tau 0.02 s)
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step, reset or seed is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
